text:
ConocoPhillips ticked down just 0.07% today, essentially flat, after a strong two-week rally of 12% that lifted the stock from $142 to $146. The lack of movement today reflects a pause in momentum rather than new negative news — crude prices remain elevated (US oil at $101.91/barrel, Brent significantly higher at $126.55), and the latest headlines continue to highlight supply disruptions that favor oil and refining companies: Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian diesel infrastructure, Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, and Middle East ship attacks keep geopolitical risk premiums baked into prices.

The stock's real strength over the past two weeks came from these tightening global oil markets and the higher diesel prices that refiners can capitalize on. Today's pause is simply a pause in an already strong trend rather than a reversal.
